title: Rethinking CAR-T neurotoxicity in glioblastoma: immune activation within a preconditioned neuroinflammatory landscape
title_zh: 重新思考胶质母细胞瘤中的CAR‑T神经毒性：免疫激活在预先调节的神经炎症环境中的作用
abstract: Abstract Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has reshaped the treatment of hematologic malignancies, leading to remarkable responses in diseases that were once considered largely refractory. However, its translation to solid tumors, and particularly to glioblastoma (GBM), has remained far more limited. GBM continues to be one of the most aggressive and treatment-resistant brain tumors, characterized by profound intratumoral heterogeneity, restricted immune cell trafficking, and a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. These features collectively constrain the efficacy of CAR-T cells within the central nervous system (CNS). In this review, we propose a conceptual framework in which CAR-T-associated neurotoxicity is not interpreted solely as a treatment-induced adverse event but rather as the consequence of immune activation occurring within a preconditioned neuroinflammatory landscape. We propose that blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, myeloid-driven inflammation, vascular dysfunction, and intracranial spatial constraints collectively establish a vulnerable CNS state that amplifies CAR-T-induced inflammatory responses. In this regard, cytokine release syndrome (CRS), immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), and tumor inflammation-associated neurotoxicity (TIAN) can be understood as interconnected and spatially modulated manifestations of a shared pathophysiological process. By integrating these processes, we provide a unified framework that links CNS-specific biology with immune-mediated toxicity across different clinical settings. This integrative perspective provides a mechanistic framework for interpreting neurotoxicity in GBM and may inform the development of safer and more effective CAR-T cell therapies. This highlights the importance of developing context-adapted CAR-T and combination strategies that account for the pre-existing tumor microenvironment and its associated baseline neuroinflammatory state, as key determinants of treatment-related toxicity.
abstract_zh: 嵌合抗原受体（CAR）T细胞疗法已重塑血液恶性肿瘤的治疗，带来显著疗效，曾被视为难治的疾病也出现了突破。然而，其向实体瘤，尤其是胶质母细胞瘤（GBM）的转化仍显有限。GBM 仍是最具侵袭性和耐药性的脑肿瘤之一，表现为显著的肿瘤内异质性、免疫细胞迁移受限以及高度免疫抑制的肿瘤微环境。这些特征共同限制了CAR‑T细胞在中枢神经系统（CNS）内的疗效。本文综述提出一个概念框架：CAR‑T相关神经毒性不应仅被视为治疗诱发的副作用，而是发生在预先调节的神经炎症环境中的免疫激活结果。我们认为血脑屏障（BBB）破坏、髓系驱动的炎症、血管功能障碍和颅内空间限制共同构成了易受损的CNS状态，放大了CAR‑T诱发的炎症反应。在此背景下，细胞因子释放综合征（CRS）、免疫效应细胞相关神经毒性综合征（ICANS）和肿瘤炎症相关神经毒性（TIAN）可被视为共享病理生理过程的相互关联且空间调控的表现。通过整合这些过程，我们提供了一个统一框架，将CNS特异性生物学与不同临床情境下的免疫介导毒性联系起来。该整合视角为解释GBM中的神经毒性提供了机制框架，并可能指导更安全、更有效的CAR‑T细胞疗法的开发。文章强调了开发适应性CAR‑T和组合策略的重要性，这些策略需考虑预先存在的肿瘤微环境及其相关的基线神经炎症状态，作为决定治疗相关毒性的关键因素。
